newsitem.title: CANADA: NEWCOURT AIMS AT RIVALS WITH COMMCORP DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NEWCOURT AIMS AT RIVALS WITH COMMCORP DEAL.

text.p: Canada's Newcourt Credit Group Inc said on Thursday it will acquire Commcorp Financial Services Inc. in a C$361 million deal to become North America's fifth-largest niche finance company.
Newcourt said the acquisition will strengthen its Canadian base against incursions by bigger U.S. rivals and allow it to challenge American competitors on their home turf.
"The combined enterprise promises to be a powerhouse in the North American asset finance market," Newcourt president and chief executive officer Steven Hudson told reporters on Thursday.
Toronto-based Newcourt will acquire all outstanding shares of Commcorp, one of Canada's largest asset finance companies, in a cash and stock deal valued at about C$361 million.

Burlington, Ontario-based Commcorp is owned 46-percent by Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, 25 percent by ORIX Corp, 13.5 percent by Canada Life Assurance Co., 13.5 percent by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan Board, and the rest by Commcorp management.
Under the agreement, CIBC would get a six-percent stake in Newcourt in exchange for the bank's 46 percent interest in Commcorp. CIBC will also get two seats on Newcourt's board.
Canada Life and Ontario Teachers' have also agreed to take Newcourt shares instead of cash.
About C$89 million of the C$361 million deal will be paid in cash, Newcourt said.

CIBC senior executive vice-president Gerry Beasley said the share exchange will enable the bank to "participate in the continued growth of one of North America's largest and most innovative asset finance companies."

Canadian Bond Rating Service confirmed its ratings for Newcourt on Thursday, saying the acquisition will benefit the company's long-term growth and provide better access to some areas of the industry.
Newcourt is a fast-growing, non-bank lender serving the commercial, corporate and institutional markets.
With operations in Canada, the United States and Australia, Newcourt's owned and managed finance assets totaled C$6.6 billion in 1996.
It reported net income of C$34 million in the six months ended June 30, up 77 percent from the first half of 1996.

Commcorp specializes in small and mid-balance business finance programs. It also provides fleet vehicle leasing and management services for major Canadian firms like CIBC, Bank of Nova Scotia and department store retailer Sears Canada Inc.
Commcorp's owned and managed finance assets totalled C$1.9 billion in 1996. Net income last year fell to C$5.8 million from C$12 million in 1995.
Newcourt said the new company would rank fifth among North American asset financiers when the deal closes on August 29.
Hudson said the merger would strengthen Newcourt in Canada to fend off competition from U.S. rivals like GE Capital, a unit of General Electric Co, and Associates First Capital Inc.
Commcorp's focus on small vendor finance, mid-market finance and fleet vehicle leasing will also help Newcourt expand abroad.
"We intend, with Commcorp's help, to export their existing programs they have in Canada, into the U.S. and international marketplace," Hudson said.
A bigger balance sheet will help Newcourt's acquisition plans for Europe and the Asia-Pacific region. "I am confident we'll have one or two of those solved in the third or fourth quarter," he said.
Newcourt said it would take a C$20 million, after-tax charge in the third quarter related to the acquisition.
Newcourt's stock closed down 0.55 to 39.95 on volume of 258,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
